verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on April 10, 2026, at approximately 8:07 p.m. ET (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Splashdown is targeted for 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) off the coast of San Diego'; R2: 'April 10, 2026... 8:07 p.m. ET/5:07 p.m. PT... Pacific Ocean off the San Diego coast'; R3: 'splash down in the Pacific Ocean at about 8:07 p.m. ET... off the coast of San Diego'; R4: 'California splashdown... off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm date, time, location in Pacific off California/San Diego coast.

verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II splashdown marks the safe return of four astronauts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II crew — NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen... welcome the Artemis II crew home'; R2: 'four astronauts... splash down... ending their journey safely'; R3: 'All four astronauts are now out of the Orion capsule... safely inside the recovery ship'
verifications.reasoning: All sources describe the splashdown as the safe return of the specific four astronauts.

verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission lasted 10 days.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Flight Day 10... began... on April 1'; R2: 'historic 10-day mission... Over 10 days'; R3: 'record-breaking 10-day mission' but 'lasted 9 days, 1 hour, 31 minutes and 35 seconds'
verifications.reasoning: Sources broadly describe as '10-day mission' and 'Flight Day 10', though one provides precise duration under 10 full days.

verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission orbited the Moon.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R1: 'historic lunar flyby'; R2: 'the crew orbited the moon'; R3: 'journey around the moon... close flyby of the far side'
verifications.reasoning: Sources contradict: R2 supports 'orbited', while R1 specifies 'flyby' and others describe circumlunar trajectory without orbit insertion.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule will land off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown... off the coast of San Diego'; R2: 'Pacific Ocean off the San Diego coast'; R3: 'splashdown... off the coast of San Diego... Pacific Ocean'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm Orion splashdown/landing location off San Diego, California.

verifications.claim: A Falcon 9 rocket is scheduled to launch from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California around 10:39 p.m. ET (7:39 p.m. PDT) on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Sources mention SpaceX Falcon 9 launch on April 10 at 7:39 PT (10:39 ET) causing sonic boom in California (R4), but no mention of Vandenberg Space Force Base.

verifications.claim: Vandenberg Space Force Base is roughly 200 miles north of the Artemis II splashdown site
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No sources mention Vandenberg, its location relative to splashdown site, or any distance.
